question: What is the approximate percentage of adolescents (10-19 years) in India as per Census 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.209**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• According to Census 2011, the population of adolescents aged 10-19 years in India was approximately 209 million.

• This number represents around 20.9% of the total population of India at that time.

• The adolescent population is a significant demographic segment, requiring focused attention on education, health, and skill development.

• Understanding the demographics of adolescents helps in planning and implementing policies for their overall development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Census 2011:**

• The Census of India is a decennial exercise that provides comprehensive data on population, demographics, economic activity, literacy, education, housing, and many other aspects.

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India since 1872.

• The total population of India as per Census 2011 was 1.21 billion.

• It helps in policy formulation, planning, and administration to ensure inclusive growth and development.

• **Adolescents:**

• Adolescence is the transitional phase of growth and development between childhood and adulthood.

• The World Health Organization (WHO) defines adolescents as individuals in the 10-19 years age group.

• This stage is characterized by rapid physical growth, cognitive development, and emotional changes.

• Focus on adolescent health, education, and social development is crucial for harnessing the demographic dividend.

• **Demographic Dividend:**

• The demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential resulting from shifts in a country’s population age structure, mainly when the working-age population is larger than the non-working-age population.

• This potential can be realized if the working-age population is healthy, educated, and gainfully employed.

• Investments in youth and adolescent development are essential to capitalize on the demographic dividend.
